messages:
alex: Heads up — I'm prototyping a routing policy shape for tiered fallback budgets and how we surface this in the Console + API. Quick brain dump and a couple questions.

maria: ye — curious about two things: 1) how we name the budget unit (tokens vs credits), 2) whether fallback counts toward tenant quota or separate 'fallback pool'.

sam: +1 on separate pool. For free tier we want aggressive auto-fallback but also a visible meter so support can see when a tenant hit fallback budget.

alex: draft DSL idea below (very rough):

```yaml
policy:
  tiers:
    free:
      prefer: [gpt-3-small]
      fallbacks: [gpt-2-quant]
      fallback_credits_per_month: 10k  # human-friendly label in Console
      fallback_enforcement: soft      # soft = degrade to cheaper variant, hard = 429/block
      surface_in_console: true
    pro:
      prefer: [gpt-3-medium, gpt-3-small]
      fallbacks: [gpt-3-small]
      fallback_credits_per_month: 100k
      fallback_enforcement: hard
  regions:
    eu:
      prefer: [gpt-3-eu]
      allow_cross_region_fallback: false
  telemetry:
    emit_fallback_reason: true  # attach reason code when fallback occurs
```

isha: I like the explicit `fallback_enforcement` flag. Implementation Q: do we count a token toward main quota AND fallback pool when fallback happens? We could double-charge metrics which would be confusing.

kevin: Implementation suggestion: when fallback happens, mark the request as `fallbacked:true` and only charge the variant that served. Then decrement fallback pool. Keep main quota unchanged. That keeps accounting simple.

maria: That makes sense, but product asked that usage alerts still trigger if customers exceed effective budget (main + fallback). Could expose combined_utilization = main_used + fallback_used for alerts.

sam: console UX — suggest two meters on tenant page: "Primary quota" and "Fallback budget" with small sparkline for last 30d and an action button to request a temporary increase.

alex: API debate: should server responses include `selected_variant` and `fallback_reason` in body, or include a header (x-redwood-variant) ? Pros: body is discoverable; header keeps response body clean for apps.

kevin: I'm leaning header for mainstream responses. But we need body field for streaming responses so clients can annotate chat history with variant. Maybe include both, with header for quick routing + body field in non-stream mode.

isha: telemetry design: we need enumerated reason codes (e.g., OUT_OF_CAPACITY, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, REGION_RESTRICTED, POLICY_PREFERENCE) so dashboards can aggregate. Also tag with `policy_version` for rollouts.

maria: rollouts UX: console should let SRE/product run a canary that flips `fallback_enforcement` for a % of traffic, and show predicted fallback cost delta. Can we compute simulation by rolling historical trace through new policy?

alex: yes — we have traces. We should add a small simulator endpoint `/v1/policies/simulate` that returns estimated fallback counts and cost delta. That can be used in the Console before applying policy.

sam: about enforcement modes: soft = always allow fallback until pool exhausted, then either hard-block or fallthrough to next compatible variant. Need a clear ordering semantics for multi-fallback lists.

kevin: propose explicit priority list with `weight` or `strict_order: true` flag. Example: `fallbacks: [{name:gpt-3-small, weight:80}, {name:gpt-2-quant, weight:20}]`. If strict_order true, ignore weights and go sequentially.

alex: ops-bot: deploying a canary schema change for policy DSL in staging now.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: policy-schema-v2 pushed to staging at 2490123499 — smoke ok.

maria: small nit — use `fallback_credits_unit` (tokens|requests|credits) so Console can toggle display unit. Free-tier support cares about requests not tokens.

isha: question about telemetry retention. We probably want fallback reason histogram at 90d at tenant-level and 13mo at aggregated level for billing disputes.

sam: agreed. Also add a flag `expose_variant_in_console` to hide internal model names for enterprise customers that request obfuscation.

kevin: last point — API surface: the policy authoring API should accept `dry_run=true` to validate and simulate. Also need error codes for policy validation failures (e.g., policy conflicts, circular region overrides).

alex: thanks everyone. Action items: kevin to draft API patch (include headers + body fields), isha to draft telemetry event schema (fallback_reason codes + policy_version), sam + maria to mock Console meters + simulation CTA, and I'll wire the simulator endpoint.

maria: noted. I'll add copy for support docs about how fallback credits are billed/displayed.

kevin: will open PR for API changes with sample responses.

ops-bot: noted. ticket created: PLAT-8764 "tiered fallback budget + simulator"

sam: :thumbsup:

alex: closing thread for now — will follow up with PR links.
